{{URL|https://olaelectric.com}} }} '''Ola Electric Mobility Limited''' is an Indian [[electric vehicle]] manufacturer headquartered in [[Bengaluru]].{{Cite web |date=2024-08-09 |title=Bhavish Aggarwal enters billionaire club as Ola Electric shares surge on market debut |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/business/story/bhavish-aggarwal-enters-billionaire-club-net-worth-144-billion-usd-ola-electric-shares-surge-on-market-debut-2579643-2024-08-09 |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=India Today |language=en}} Founded in 2017 by [[Bhavish Aggarwal]], the company designs and manufactures [[Electric motorcycles and scooters|electric two-wheelers]], including the Ola S1 in three variants named Ola S1 Air, Ola S1X and S1 Pro. It has its manufacturing facility located in [[Krishnagiri]], [[Tamil Nadu]]. The company also produces [[battery cell]]s at its manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu, which supplies [[energy storage]] products for its vehicles and other applications.{{Cite web |date=2024-07-01 |title=India-based Ola Electric ramps up cell manufacturing, develops solid-state battery |url=https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20240701VL201/ola-electric-manufacturing-ipo-unicorn-electric-two-wheeler.html |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=DIGITIMES |language=en}} As of 2023, the company led the electric scooter market in India, with a 30% share.{{Cite web |date=2023-09-20 |title=Ola Electric eyes IPO filing by Oct-end to raise up to $700 mn: Report |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/ipo-corner/story/ola-electric-eyes-ipo-filing-by-oct-end-to-raise-up-to-700-mn-report-399068-2023-09-20 |access-date=2023-09-21 |website=Business Today |language=en}} ==History== ===2017–2019=== Ola Electric was established in 2017 as a wholly owned subsidiary of ANI Technologies, the parent entity of [[Ola Cabs]].{{cite news |title=The big electric scooter battle |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/enterprise/the-big-electric-scooter-battle/105440 |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=Fortune India |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Ola: Ola Electric gets $250m funding from SoftBank |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/ola-electric-gets-250m-funding-from-softbank/articleshow/70050081.cms |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=The Economic Times}} The company was started to reduce emission and fuel dependency of Ola's cabs, and shift to mass electric mobility; a pilot program was launched in [[Nagpur]] in May 2017 by setting up [[charging stations]] across the city and procuring [[electric car|electric cabs]], [[Electric bus|e-buses]], and [[Electric rickshaw|e-rickshaws]] from [[OEM]] partners.{{cite news |last1= Peermohamed |first1=Alnoor |title=Ola kicks off pilot of its electric mass mobility project in Nagpur |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ola-kicks-off-pilot-of-its-electric-mass-mobility-project-in-nagpur-117052601413_1.html |access-date=23 November 2021 |work=Business Standard India |date=27 May 2017}}{{cite news |title=Introducing Ola Electric |url=https://blog.olacabs.com/introducing-ola-electric/ |access-date=23 November 2021 |work=blog.olacabs.com}} In April 2018, it announced that it aims to have 1 million electric vehicles in its cab service by 2022.{{cite news |last1=Peermohamed |first1=Alnoor |title=Ola aligns with Softbank's dream of one million electric vehicles |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ola-aligns-with-softbank-s-dream-of-one-million-electric-vehicles-118041600293_1.html |access-date=23 November 2021 |work=Business Standard India |date=17 April 2018}} Between December 2018 and January 2019, founder [[Bhavish Aggarwal]] bought a 92.5% stake in Ola Electric from ANI Technologies at a valuation of {{INR}}1 [[lakh]] (about US$1,400 then), and Ola Electric was [[Corporate spin-off|spun-off]] as a separate entity. ANI Technologies continued to hold a 7.5% stake in Ola Electric for allowing the use of "Ola" [[brand equity|brand name]].{{cite news |title=The Curious Case Of Bhavish Aggarwal And Ola Electric |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/the-curious-case-of-bhavish-aggarwal-and-ola-electric-4447411.html |access-date=23 November 2021 |work=Moneycontrol |language=en}} In February 2019, Ola Electric raised {{USD}}56 million from [[Tiger Global]] and [[Matrix Partners|Matrix India]].{{cite news |title=India's Ola spins out a dedicated EV business — and it just raised $56M from investors |url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/02/28/ola-ev-business-ola-electric-mobility/ |access-date=23 November 2021 |work=TechCrunch}} The company announced on 6 May 2019 that [[Ratan Tata]] had invested an undisclosed amount in Ola Electric as part of its [[Series A round]] of funding.{{cite web |last1=Bansal |first1=Varsha |title=Ratan Tata raises stake in Ola, invests in fledgling electric vehicle business |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/ratan-tata-raises-stake-in-ola-invests-in-fledgling-electric-vehicle-business-1557123393182.html|website=Mint|access-date=7 May 2019 |language=en |date=6 May 2019}} It raised $250 million from SoftBank during [[Series B round]] funding in July 2019, at a valuation of over $1 billion.{{cite web |last1=Bansal |first1=Varsha |title=Ola Electric races to unicorn status with $250-million fundraise from SoftBank |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/ola-electric-races-to-unicorn-status-with-250-million-fundraise-from-softbank-1562057141398.html |website=mint |language=en |date=2 July 2019}} ===2020–present=== [[File:Black_OLA_Electric_scooters.jpg|thumb|Ola scooters fresh out of assembly line]] In May 2020, Ola Electric acquired Etergo, an [[Amsterdam]]-based [[crowdfunded]] electric scooter manufacturer, for €3.75 million in a [[distress sale]].{{cite news |last1=S.H |first1=Salman |title=Ola's Electric Ambitions Hinge On A Brewing Lawsuit Stemming From An Acquisition |url=https://inc42.com/features/olas-etergo-acquisition-global-dream-faces-lawsuit-angry-investors/ |access-date=2 August 2024 |work=Inc42 Media |date=24 November 2020 |language=en}} Ola Electric announced that it would launch its own line of electric scooters in India by 2021.{{cite news |last1=Bhalla |first1=Tarush |title=Ola Electric acquires Etergo, looks to launch electric scooters in India by 2021 |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/ola-electric-acquires-etergo-looks-to-launch-electric-scooters-in-india-by-2021-11590576268370.html |access-date=23 November 2021 |work=mint |date=27 May 2020 |language=en}} In December 2020, the company announced its plan to set up the world's largest two wheeler factory (called the Future Factory) in [[Tamil Nadu]] at a cost of {{INRconvert|2400|c|mode=historical|year=2020}} after signing a memorandum with the [[Government of Tamil Nadu]].{{cite news |last1=Abrar |first1=Peerzada |title=Ola to invest Rs 2,400 crore for 'world's largest' e-scooter factory |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ola-to-set-up-world-s-largest-scooter-factory-to-invest-rs-2-400-cr-120121400436_1.html |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=Business Standard India |date=14 December 2020}} It acquired a 500-acre land in [[Pochampalli, Tamil Nadu|Pochampalli]], [[Krishnagiri District]] in January 2021; the construction work for the factory began in late February.{{cite news |title=Ola Electric factory almost ready as company gears up for e-scooter launch |url=https://auto.hindustantimes.com/auto/news/ola-electric-factory-almost-ready-as-company-gears-up-for-e-scooter-launch-41628070089193.html |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=Hindustan Times Auto News |date=4 August 2021 |language=en}} [[File:OLA S1 Pro Gen 1 Electric Scooter.jpg|thumb|OLA S1 Pro Gen 1 Electric Scooter]] [[File:Ola electric scooter.jpg|thumb|Ola electric scooter]] Ola Electric received 500,000 bookings for scooters in the first month of availability.{{cite news |date=20 August 2021 |author=Anirban Mitra | title=Electric Scooter News: How Ola, Simple e-scooters started solid, clocked record bookings {{!}} |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/auto/bikes/how-ola-simple-e-scooters-started-solid-clocked-record-bookings/articleshow/85488160.cms |work=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=20 August 2021 |language=en}} Ola Electric started delivering its S1 and S1 Pro models in December 2021 with the deliveries of 100 scooters in Bengaluru and Chennai, although some promised features were not enabled in initial deliveries.{{Cite news|title=Ola Electric delivers first 100 scooters without some promised features|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/ola-electric-delivers-first-100-scooters-without-some-promised-features/articleshow/88304096.cms|access-date=2021-12-17}}{{Cite web|date=2021-12-16|title=Ola Electric Commences S1, S1 Pro Scooter Deliveries in Bengaluru and Chennai|url=https://www.news18.com/news/auto/ola-electric-commences-s1-s1-pro-scooter-deliveries-in-bengaluru-and-chennai-4561130.html|access-date=2021-12-17|website=News18|language=en}} Ola Electric raised more than $200 million from Falcon Edge, [[SoftBank Group]] and others at a valuation of $3 billion in September 2021.{{Cite news|title=Ola Electric gets $200 million funding at $3 billion valuation|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/ola-electric-gets-200-million-funding-at-3-billion-valuation/articleshow/86648009.cms|access-date=2021-12-17}} In December the same year, it raised $53 million in an investment round led by Singaporean investment firm, [[Temasek Holdings|Temasek]].{{Cite web|last=Agarwal|first=Ankit|date=2021-12-08|title=Ola Electric raises $53 mn in round led by Temasek, valued at $2.7 bn|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/start-ups/ola-electric-raises-53-mn-in-round-led-by-temasek-valued-at-2-7-bn-11638974023410.html|access-date=2021-12-17|website=mint|language=en}} In January 2022, Ola Electric raised {{USD}}200 million from multiple investors at a valuation of {{USD}}5 billion.{{cite news |title=Ola Electric raises $200 million in funding at a valuation of $5 billion |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/companies/ola-electric-raises-200-million-in-funding-at-a-valuation-of-5-billion-12228652.htm |access-date=27 January 2022 |work=cnbctv18.com |date=24 January 2022 |language=en}} In late March 2022, Ola made a strategic investment in Israel-based battery technology company [[StoreDot]] to incorporate and manufacture its XFC (extreme fast charging) battery technologies for future vehicles in India.{{cite news |title=Ola Electric makes strategic investment in fast-charging tech company StoreDot |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/ola-electric-makes-strategic-investment-in-fast-charging-firm-storedot/articleshow/90356230.cms |access-date=2 August 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=21 March 2022}} In the wake of a [[Plug-in electric vehicle fire incidents|fire incident]] in its scooter in [[Pune]] on 26 March, the company recalled a batch of 1,441 scooters in April as a "pre-emptive measure".{{cite news |title=Ola Electric recalls 1,441 units of electric two-wheelers |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/ola-electric-recalling-1441-units-of-electric-two-wheelers/article65350610.ece |access-date=2 August 2024 |work=The Hindu |date=24 April 2022 |language=en-IN}} On 20 June 2022, Ola Electric teased its first sedan electric car.{{Cite web |date=2022-06-20 |title=Ola Electric teases its first electric car; likely to launch in 2023 |url=https://auto.hindustantimes.com/auto/electric-vehicles/ola-electric-teases-its-first-electric-car-likely-to-launch-in-2023-41655726017650.html |access-date=2022-06-21 |website=Hindustan Times Auto News |language=en}} However, two years later, the company scrapped its plan to launch electric cars, choosing to focus on electric scooters and motorcycles.{{cite news |last1=Aditi |first1=Shah |last2=Kalra |first2=Aditya |title=SoftBank-backed Ola Electric suspends India car project to focus on scooters, bikes, sources say |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/softbank-backed-ola-electric-suspends-india-car-project-focus-scooters-bikes-2024-07-25/ |access-date=15 August 2024 |work=Reuters |date=25 July 2024}} In July 2022, CEO Bhavish Aggarwal announced that the company was building Battery Innovation Center (BIC) in Bangalore, which would be Asia's largest cell R&D facility, with an investment of $500 million.{{cite web | url=https://auto.hindustantimes.com/auto/electric-vehicles/ola-electric-building-ev-cell-r-d-facility-in-bengaluru-with-500-mn-investment-41658143413068.html | title=Ola Electric building EV cell R&D facility in Bengaluru with $500 mn investment | work=Hindustan Times| date=18 July 2022 }} In October 2023, the company raised $140 million in equity and $240 million in debt, at a valuation of $5.4 billion, to set up a [[lithium-ion battery]] manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu called Ola Gigafactory.{{cite news |title=Ola Electric closes $240 million in debt financing to set up lithium-ion cell factory |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/ola-electric-closes-240-million-in-debt-financing-to-set-up-lithium-ion-cell-factory/articleshow/104728608.cms |access-date=2 August 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=26 October 2023}}{{Cite news |date=2023-06-21 |title=Ola Electric commences construction of India's largest Gigafactory in Tamil Nadu |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/business-economy/companies/ola-electric-commences-construction-of-indias-largest-gigafactory-in-tamil-nadu-article-101168361 |access-date=2023-06-24 |website=TimesNow |language=en}} On 2 August 2024, Ola Electric launched its [[initial public offering]] (IPO) and raised {{INR}}5,500 crore. Existing investors, including founder Aggarwal, sold 84.9 million shares in the IPO.{{Cite news |date=2024-07-28 |title=Ola Electric Mobility: EV maker to launch IPO on August 2 to raise Rs 5,500 crore |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/ola-electric-mobility-ev-maker-to-launch-ipo-on-august-2-to-raise-rs-5500-crore/articleshow/112081556.cms |access-date=2024-07-28 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}{{cite web | url=https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/ola-electric-holds-a-battery-secret-on-road-to-ipo-11711020114854.html | title=Ola Electric holds a battery secret on road to IPO | date=21 March 2024| work=Mint }} On 15 August 2024, Ola Electric unveiled the [[prototype]] of its first electric motorcycle series, named Roadster, which was announced to be launched in three variants in 2025.{{cite news |title=Ola Electric launches e-motorcycle series 'Roadster' starting at Rs 74,999 |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/ola-electric-unveils-roadster-series-its-first-e-motorcycle-12797354.html |access-date=21 August 2024 |work=Moneycontrol}} In September 2024, Aggarwal announced that Ola Electric will unveil its [[Electric rickshaw|electric three-wheeler]] later that year.{{Cite web |date=2024-09-05 |title=Ola Electric is working to bring its three-wheeler to market soon, says Bhavish Aggarwal |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/auto/bhavish-aggarwal-ola-electric-share-price-three-wheeler-launch-ev-market-share-new-launches-19471422.htm |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}} In May 2026, the company received regulatory approval for a new electric scooter with a top speed around 70kmph.{{Cite web |last= |title=Ola Electric gets nod for commercial e-scooter from ARAI, eyes fleet mobility push |url=https://auto.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/two-wheelers/ola-electric-launches-new-commercial-e-scooter-amid-rising-fuel-prices/131345745 |access-date=2026-05-27 |website=ETAuto.com |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2026-05-27 |title=Ola Electric eyes commercial EV launch for gig workers amid quick commerce boom |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/ola-electric-eyes-commercial-ev-launch-for-gig-workers-amid-quick-commerce-boom/articleshow/131353633.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-27 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} ==Production== [[File:OLA_Electric_scooter_battery_assembly.jpg|thumb|Ola scooter assembly line]] Ola Electric operates a 500-acre automated complex, called the Ola Future Factory, in [[Pochampalli, Tamil Nadu]].{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-04-25 |title=Watch: Here's a look inside Ola's electric scooter Futurefactory |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/auto-news/watch-heres-a-look-inside-olas-electric-scooter-futurefactory/videoshow/91077894.cms |access-date=2026-05-27 |website=The Economic Times |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Maidas |first=Meenakshi |date=29 May 2025 |title=Indian two-wheeler maker Ola Electric's quarterly loss widens, targets profitability in FY26 |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/india/indian-two-wheeler-maker-ola-electrics-quarterly-loss-widens-2025-05-29/ |website=Reuters}} It has deployed automated robots in its [[weld line|welding]] and painting lines, and battery and motor [[assembly line]]s.{{cite news |title=Ola to deploy ABB’s robotics, automation solutions at EV manufacturing facility |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/companies/ola-to-deploy-abbs-robotics-automation-solutions-at-ev-manufacturing-facility-7184371/ |access-date=17 September 2024 |work=The Indian Express |date=11 February 2021 |language=en}} In 2021, it announced that it would employ only female workers on its manufacturing floor.{{cite news |last1=Baba |first1=Moyuru |title=Indian startup Ola opens all-female electric scooter factory |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Business/Startups/Indian-startup-Ola-opens-all-female-electric-scooter-factory |access-date=17 September 2024 |work=Nikkei Asia |date=23 September 2021}} The first electric scooter was manufactured on 15 August 2021.{{cite web |last1=Mohile |first1=Shally Seth |title=Ola Electric to ride into two-wheeler market with scooter launch on Aug 15 |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ola-electric-to-ride-into-two-wheeler-market-with-scooter-launch-on-aug-15-121080301492_1.html |website=Business Standard India |date=3 August 2021}} By January 2022, it was producing nearly a thousand electric scooters daily.{{cite web |title=Ola commences construction of mega factory on 500-acre site in Tamil Nadu, eyes production soon |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/auto/ola-commences-construction-of-mega-factory-on-500-acre-site-in-tamil-nadu-eyes-production-soon-8425271.htm |website=www.cnbctv18.com |language=en |date=25 February 2021}} As of 2024, Ola Electric sources batteries for its electric scooters from [[LG Energy Solution]] and [[CATL]]. The company has announced that it would transition to using batteries from its own manufacturing facility, the Ola Gigafactory in Pochampalli, which is anticipated to commence commercial production of [[lithium-ion batteries]] in 2025.{{cite news |title=Ola Electric working on building solid-state batteries: Bhavish Aggarwal |url=https://www.business-standard.com/industry/auto/working-on-building-solid-state-batteries-in-early-stage-ola-electric-ceo-124062900625_1.html |access-date=17 September 2024 |work=Business Standard}} ==Reception== In 2022, reports surfaced about a [[Toxic workplace|hostile work culture]] within the company.{{cite news |last1=Desai |first1=Prathik |date=18 May 2022 |title=Unreal deadlines, no autonomy, high-level exits: Ola Electric's work culture under scanner |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/business/unreal-deadlines-no-autonomy-high-level-exits-ola-electrics-work-culture-under-scanner-1110120.html |access-date=15 August 2024 |work=Deccan Herald |language=en}}{{cite news |last1=Sharma |first1=Niharika |date=19 October 2022 |title=What has turned Ola Electric into a toxic workplace? |url=https://qz.com/bhavish-aggarwal-is-turning-ola-electric-toxic-employer-1849675814 |access-date=15 August 2024 |work=Quartz |language=en}} In March 2023, following criticism over safety defects in its [[Motorcycle fork|front fork design]],{{cite news |last1=Sachdev |first1=Alisha |title=How Ola wilfully endangered its riders |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/how-ola-wilfully-endangered-lives-11678893874021.html |access-date=15 August 2024 |work=Mint |date=12 April 2023}}{{cite news |last1=Charan |first1=Parth |title=Opinion {{!}} Ola Electric’s faulty front fork design highlights a history of problems with its scooters |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/opinion-ola-electrics-faulty-front-fork-design-highlights-a-history-of-problems-with-its-scooters-10286001.html |access-date=15 August 2024 |work=Moneycontrol |date=21 March 2023}} Ola Electric announced that it would replace the front fork arms of its S1 and S1 Pro series scooters at no cost.{{cite news |title=Ola offers free front fork replacement for Ola S1 and S1 Pro scooters |url=https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/ola-offers-free-front-fork-replacement-for-ola-s1-and-s1-pro-scooters-11678793915706.html |access-date=16 August 2024 |work=Mint |date=14 March 2023}}{{cite news |last1=John |first1=Nirmal |title=Replacement? Recall? Upgrade? Ola Electric’s word jugglery in the S1 Pro front-fork arm controversy |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/prime/transportation/replacement-recall-upgrade-ola-electrics-word-jugglery-in-the-s1-pro-front-fork-controversy/primearticleshow/98711111.cms |access-date=16 August 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=17 March 2023}} In a 2024 presentation, Ola's CEO stated that the company is the world's largest electric two-wheeler manufacturer with a [[fine print]] reading "excluding China". Commentators noted that the world's five largest electric two-wheeler companies are all Chinese, having a combined global market share of 72%, and debunked other misleading claims in the presentation.{{Cite web |date=25 August 2024 |title=Why the Chinese EV sector is not a ‘footnote’ |url=https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/ola-electric-bhavish-aggarwal-evs-electric-vehicles-india-chinese-evs-byd-tvs-motor-two-wheelers-electric-cars-ice-cars-11724563173073.html|work=Mint}}{{Cite web |last=Anupam |first=Suprita |date=2024-08-17 |title=Fact-Checking Ola’s Sankalp: Do Bhavish Aggarwal’s Claims Hold Up? |url=https://inc42.com/features/ola-electric-sankalp-krutrim-bhavish-aggarwal-claims/ |access-date=2024-08-27 |website=Inc42 Media |language=en}} In August 2024, Ola Electric was criticized for [[plagiarism]] after it used a competitor's advertising photographs with Ola Electric motorcycles substituted for those of the competitor.{{Cite news |last=Sood |first=Utkarsh |date=12 September 2024 |title=All that glitters is not gold: Ola e-motorcycles slammed upon launch |url=https://newatlas.com/motorcycles/ola-e-motorcycles-problems/ |work=New Atlas }}{{Cite news |last=Momin |first=Aamir Ola Electric Mobility Limited is an Indian electric vehicle manufacturer headquartered in Bengaluru. Founded in 2017 by Bhavish Aggarwal, the company designs and manufactures electric two-wheelers, including the Ola S1 in three variants named Ola S1 Air, Ola S1X and S1 Pro. It has its manufacturing facility located in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu.
The company also produces battery cells at its manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu, which supplies energy storage products for its vehicles and other applications. As of 2023, the company led the electric scooter market in India, with a 30% share.
